comments.author: deependujha
comments.body:
Hi @guarin @morestart, thanks for opening the issue.
After digging into this, here's a full breakdown of what's happening and how the fix works.

---

### What's causing the warning

The warning itself states it cleanly: `[rank1]: UserWarning: The AccumulateGrad node's stream does not match the stream of the node that produced the incoming gradient.`

The warning fires inside `torch/csrc/autograd/input_buffer.cpp` when `opt_consumer_stream` (the stream the AccumulateGrad node was created on) doesn't match `opt_producer_stream` (the stream currently producing the incoming gradient).

https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/c5d8d5e61e1ab44dcb85ad975b60009dece95c02/torch/csrc/autograd/input_buffer.cpp#L310-L324

Since Fabric initialized DDP on a side-stream, the AccumulateGrad nodes were created on that side-stream. Normal forward/backward runs on the default stream, so every backward triggers the mismatch. `del loss` and `del output` don't help because DDP's C++ Reducer holds its own independent reference to these nodes, clearing Python-side references doesn't destroy them.

https://github.com/Lightning-AI/pytorch-lightning/blob/932b7e3e76ea96481003ceacb13c3e8194f281d2/src/lightning/fabric/strategies/ddp.py#L124-L130

The key line in the warning explains it:

> *"This mismatch is caused by an AccumulateGrad node created prior to the current iteration being kept alive... or if you are using DDP, which will stash a reference to the node."*

---

### Why Fabric triggers it but plain PyTorch doesn't

Looking at `setup_module` in `DDPStrategy`:

```python
# original code
ctx = torch.cuda.stream(torch.cuda.Stream())  # <-- new side-stream
with ctx:
    return DistributedDataParallel(...)
```

Fabric was initializing DDP on a **new non-default stream**. This was intentional, the PyTorch CUDA Graphs docs explicitly require DDP to be initialized on a side-stream for whole-network capture:
https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/2.12/notes/cuda.html#id5

But in normal training (no CUDA graphs), all forward and backward passes run on the **default stream**. So every backward pass hits `AccumulateGrad` nodes that were registered on a different stream → warning.

Plain PyTorch users call `DistributedDataParallel(model, ...)` directly with no stream context, so DDP initializes on the default stream and there's no mismatch.

---

### What I tried that didn't work

- `del loss` after `fabric.backward(loss)`: no effect. The graph reference is held by DDP's C++ Reducer, not Python.
- `del loss, output`: same, still fires.
- `torch.cuda.stream(torch.cuda.default_stream())` around `fabric.setup()` in user code: no effect because Fabric defers the actual `DistributedDataParallel` construction to `setup_module`, which runs after the user's stream context has already exited.

---

### The fix

Use `torch.cuda.is_current_stream_capturing()` to detect whether we're inside a CUDA graph capture at DDP initialization time, and branch accordingly:

```python
capturing = torch.cuda.is_current_stream_capturing()
if capturing:
    # CUDA graph whole-network capture requires DDP on a side-stream.
    # Stream mismatch is intentional here; suppress the warning.
    ctx = torch.cuda.stream(torch.cuda.Stream())
    torch.autograd.graph.set_warn_on_accumulate_grad_stream_mismatch(False)
else:
    # Normal training: default stream prevents the AccumulateGrad mismatch.
    ctx = torch.cuda.stream(torch.cuda.default_stream())
```

This means:
- Normal DDP training: no warning, correct behavior, no user action needed.
- CUDA graph capture: side-stream preserved as required, warning suppressed since the mismatch is expected and benign in that context.

---

### Resources

- PyTorch CUDA Graphs docs (why side-stream is needed for DDP + graph capture): https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/2.12/notes/cuda.html#id5
- PyTorch AccumulateGrad stream check source: [torch/csrc/autograd/input_buffer.cpp](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/c5d8d5e61e1ab44dcb85ad975b60009dece95c02/torch/csrc/autograd/input_buffer.cpp#L310-L324)
